framework_rationale: The solution imports tensorcircuit and uses it for all core quantum computation: configuring TensorCircuit's JAX backend, complex128 dtype, and custom Cotengra tensor-network contractor, constructing tc.Circuit instances with single-qubit (rx, ry, rz) and two-qubit (rxx, ryy, rzz) gates, and evaluating Pauli expectations via circuit.expectation(..., enable_lightcone=True). The other imports (typing, numpy, jax, optax, cotengra) are standard scientific, optimization, and tensor-network contraction support libraries rather than other quantum frameworks.
cheating_rationale: There is no evidence of cheating, hardcoded answers, hidden oracle access, evaluator exploitation, or test/reward tampering. All circuit structure, Pauli observables, seeds, and hyperparameters are read dynamically from config, and the reported optimization metrics are consistent with genuine variational optimization of the specified observables.
fidelity_rationale: The implementation faithfully matches the problem specification. It extracts exact backward causal light cones for each Pauli term from config['gate_tape'], maps shared active parameters consistently across cones, prepares the |+> initial state on each active qubit via ry(pi/2)|0>, applies all kept single- and two-qubit gates using TensorCircuit's matching exp(-i theta P / 2) convention, evaluates the weighted local Pauli objective, and minimizes -local_objective(theta). Parameter initialization draws the full parameter_count Gaussian vector per restart using seed + 100000 + restart_index and standard deviation initial_parameter_scale before slicing active parameters, preserving exact per-parameter RNG alignment. Optimization uses Optax Adam at the configured learning rate for exactly max_steps iterations without early stopping, recording the pre-update local objective at each step and returning {'observable_history': ndarray} of shape (n_restarts, max_steps).
implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation errors were found. Backward light-cone extraction, active-parameter indexing, state preparation, gate application, expectation evaluation, gradient computation, Adam updates, pre-update history logging, and edge-case handling (empty restarts/steps, identity Pauli terms, or zero active parameters) are all mathematically and programmatically sound.
